themes_detail.label: Dead and dying trees surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead/Dying Tree complaints spiked to 22 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 5.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks (up 319%), signaling a potential disease outbreak, storm damage, or environmental stress affecting the district's urban forest—a concern flagged repeatedly in community board budget requests for forestry services.
evidence: 22 Dead/Dying Tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.2-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 7.95, severity: high)
319% increase from 8-week average; consistent with long-standing community board requests for forestry and street tree maintenance
Correlates with Damaged Tree complaints (413 total over 90 days), suggesting district-wide tree health crisis
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department arborist about disease patterns or recent storm impact in Tottenville/Great Kills; obtain canopy health assessment data
Canvass residents and community board members about visible tree decline; investigate whether recent weather events or infrastructure work triggered die-off

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Park complaints skyrocketed to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week (up 3100%, z-score: 11.72)—the district's most statistically extreme spike—indicating a sudden change in park usage, events, or enforcement that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 Park Noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72, highest severity flagged)
No prior Reddit discussion or news coverage suggests this is newly emerging
Correlates with elevated Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints (16 last week vs 6.2 baseline, up 156%)
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated complaints; contact Parks Department and NYPD 120th Precinct about new events, gatherings, or noise source
Interview residents near affected parks about frequency, timing, and source of noise (groups, equipment, construction)

themes_detail.label: Street and sidewalk noise spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints jumped to 19 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.2 per week (up 485%, z-score: 5.78), paired with a spike in Missing Street Signs (7 vs 1.2 baseline) and elevated Non-Emergency Police calls (16 vs 6.2), suggesting potential street activity disruption or infrastructure work.
evidence: 19 Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.2-complaint weekly baseline (485% increase, z-score: 5.78)
7 Missing Street Sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2-complaint weekly baseline (460% increase, z-score: 4.8), suggesting possible road work or signage removal
16 Non-Emergency Police complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.2-complaint weekly baseline (156% increase, z-score: 4.09) indicates broader street-level disorder
reporting_angles: Cross-check DOT work orders and construction permits for active street projects in Tottenville/Great Kills; contact agency about duration and scope
Survey residents on which streets are affected; determine whether noise is from construction, street vending, or other activity

themes_detail.label: Air quality complaints rise
themes_detail.summary: Air Quality complaints reached 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 233% from a baseline of 1.5 per week (z-score: 4.95), suggesting a potential pollution event, industrial activity, or emissions source emerging in the district.
evidence: 5 Air Quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5-complaint weekly baseline (233% increase, z-score: 4.95)
Great Kills and Tottenville are near Staten Island's industrial zones and Arthur Kill waterway; industrial sources plausible
Correlates with Lot Condition spike (4 complaints vs 0.2 baseline) and long-standing community board requests for illegal dumping enforcement
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and state DEC for air quality monitoring data; identify potential industrial or construction sources
Interview residents about odors, visibility, and health impacts; cross-check with any facility or construction activity filed with DOB or ULURP

themes_detail.label: Lot condition complaints emerge
themes_detail.summary: Lot Condition complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week (up 1500%, z-score: 5.67), aligning with long-standing community board requests for illegal dumping enforcement, suggesting possible dumping or property neglect in the district.
evidence: 4 Lot Condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2-complaint weekly baseline (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Community board has repeatedly requested increased illegal dumping law enforcement, indicating persistent local concern
Correlates with Air Quality spike and elevated Non-Emergency Police calls, suggesting property disorder cluster
reporting_angles: Identify specific lots generating complaints via 311 data; conduct on-site inspection to document dumping or deterioration
Contact Department of Sanitation and Enforcement about illegal dumping investigations and enforcement activity in district
